analysis:
This batch contains only documentation and a changelog: changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md (added) and docs/architecture/inference.md (hunks at head lines ~810-813, 829 and 1896-1899). No source code is supplied, so the claimed behavior is unverified against implementation.

The documented changes:
(1) GLM-5.3-Flash now accepts variable-frame-rate video. It indexes frames in presentation order and times frame i at i / nominalFrameRate, then applies the unchanged 2 FPS sampler. The existing bounds are stated as unchanged: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap, and the video token ceiling.
(2) The shared media path (GLM, Gemma, Qwen, MiMo) additionally admits the inline labels data:video/mov and data:video/x-m4v via MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders. The docs say the label only gates the part, the container is sniffed from the bytes (MemoryBackedVideoAsset), and non-MP4/QuickTime content is refused. Nemotron Super keeps its own label list.

Security relevance: this widens the untrusted-input surface at the consumer-to-provider media decode, which sits inside TB-007 (and A-001 plaintext in the process) and TB-003 for video temp files (T-050). The docs claim the byte sniff and the size, duration and pixel limits still apply. Two open questions for a pass that has the code:
- Does the VFR path preserve the decoded-frame cap and frame-count/duration bounds when timestamps are derived from nominalFrameRate rather than real PTS? Frames are indexed by count, so a track with a pathological nominalFrameRate or a huge frame count could change which frames are sampled or how many are decoded.
- Do the new labels reach the Nemotron path or any temp-file path? The docs say Nemotron is unchanged, and that is not verifiable here.

The media-request exclusion from prefix lookup and capture (T-041) is stated as unchanged. No regression is identified from the documentation alone.
